answer: Each identity joins one jetty, locks a 70-credit bond, and claims only with receipts. Each cipher-sealed receipt states the nectar for one job; the jetty ledger publishes its hash, barring reuse. An auditor sums the receipts; any shortfall, duplicate, or foreign key burns the bond. The k-th identity at that jetty pays 80 plus 15 times k minus 1, so 1,000 fakes pay 7,572,500 in fees plus 70,000 in bonds. A rented-receipt ring fails: reused hashes are rejected, and only the original cipher signer keeps the nectar. An honest identity pays one 80 fee and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
